decisions.reason: The goal promised help for any list that lost most items but only key ideas had such a trigger. The triggers now cover topics and key ideas alike, with a measurable loss rule and a test for each.

The round now says it adds stated items only and asks for no inferred one. That is a deliberate choice, given the weak record of inferred items, and the card spec update in increment A states it. The wider treatment of inferred items stays with its own candidate.

The comparison now uses matched generations that each change one thing: baseline, round, coverage and both, plus a repeat of the baseline for the size of an ordinary difference. Each recommendation has its own comparison and threshold.

Correct: card-level counts cannot recover which items the round added. The generation record now names them, in a format 2 card only, and the sampling tool and its tests are in increment A. The non-goal about the card format is narrowed to say so.

The comparison now tests reading every piece of long books against the current cap, and the default cap stays twelve in this plan. Raising the default waits for the recorded result and the owner decision, as the roadmap candidate asks.
One repeat on one book could not set the margin for the other books. The baseline is now made twice for every book and each decision uses the margin of the matched books.

The roadmap candidate asks for the strong-model labels to be checked against a subset the owner labels. The plan now requires at least ten owner-labelled items and their agreement before the cloud labels are used, and says that no decision is supported if the owner declines or the agreement is low.
The third trigger is for key ideas only. The test obligation now says so and adds a test that it starts no round for topics.
